claims.text: The starting material is an as-cast HfZrTiTa0.53 refractory high-entropy alloy.
The baseline quasi-static yield strength, compressive strength, and fracture strain are 786 MPa, 1314 MPa, and 13.5%, respectively.
The proposed treatment is solutionizing at approximately 1400°C followed by aging at approximately 500°C for 4–8 hours.
This treatment will precipitate nanoscale L12 or similarly ordered second-phase particles in HfZrTiTa0.53.
The treatment will produce a fine, homogeneous precipitate dispersion within the alloy's BCC matrix.
The nanoscale precipitates will promote load sharing and inhibit dislocation glide.
The precipitates will act as dislocation obstacles and sources of back stress, thereby increasing strain hardening.
The precipitates will redistribute strain and disrupt the formation and propagation of adiabatic shear bands.
The aged alloy will have higher dynamic yield and compressive strengths than the baseline alloy.
The aged alloy's compressive strength may approach or exceed 2300 MPa under dynamic loading.
The aged alloy will exhibit greater uniform deformation and a fracture strain exceeding 13.5%.
The aged alloy will have improved resistance to adiabatic shear-band formation.
The aged alloy will exhibit a more gradual impact-induced energy-release profile.
The predicted improvements apply during adiabatic dynamic compression at strain rates of 1000–3000 s^-1.
The precipitation effect may be less pronounced at quasi-static strain rates or substantially different temperatures.
Nonoptimal aging may cause precipitate coarsening or embrittlement.
A matched experiment will compare solutionized-only and solutionized-plus-aged specimens from the same alloy batch under identical dynamic compression conditions.
The hypothesis is falsified if aging produces no statistically significant improvement in dynamic strength, deformation before failure, and delayed or reduced shear-band formation.

contradictions.description: The stated baseline is as-cast or vaguely 'as-cast/quasi-statically processed,' whereas the experimental control is solutionized-only. Solutionizing can alter the baseline microstructure and properties, so the proposed control is not necessarily the stated as-cast baseline.
